title: free-disk-space decisions
description: Choices the code makes that a change could undo, and questions only the owner can answer. Where the code or README gives no reason, none is recorded.

entities.title: Which day protects dev artifacts
entities.summary: Dev artifacts modified today are kept, and today starts at midnight UTC (Atlantic/Reykjavik) for every user, whatever the Mac's own time zone.
entities.context: clean_dev keeps any artifact with something modified since today_start_ts, which is midnight UTC; the README and the skill both say "today (Atlantic/Reykjavik)". The binary is published through Homebrew and release tarballs, so it may run in any time zone. East of UTC the protected day starts after local midnight (at 10:00 at UTC+10), so build output from that morning can be deleted; west of UTC it starts on the previous local day, which only keeps more.

options.title: Keep the fixed UTC day
options.consequences: The same rule everywhere, as documented; users east of UTC get less protection than the word today suggests.

options.title: Use the Mac's local day
options.consequences: Today means what the user expects; the README, the skill and the KEEP_TODAY text change, and the tests need a time zone.

options.title: Use a rolling window (such as the last 24 hours)
options.consequences: Independent of time zones; changes the documented rule.

entities.title: Whether FDS_TOOLS stays in release builds
entities.summary: The test seam that redirects /usr/bin/ditto, /usr/bin/xattr, /bin/launchctl and the other absolute tool paths is read by release builds too.
entities.context: util::tool rewrites any absolute program path to $FDS_TOOLS/<name> when that variable is set; its comment says it is there so tests can fake macOS tools. It is not behind cfg(test), so in normal use whatever sets FDS_TOOLS in the environment decides which programs compress, dedupe, trash and the daemon install run.

options.title: Keep it in every build
options.consequences: Tests and manual experiments can fake tools without rebuilding; the environment can redirect what the tool runs.

options.title: Compile it only for tests
options.consequences: Release builds always run the system's tools; manual runs against fake tools need a test build.

entities.title: Change files only by swapping in a verified copy
entities.summary: compress and dedupe never write into a user's file: they build a temp copy beside it, check it, and rename it over the original.
entities.context: Both commands replace files the user may care about, on a file system that also holds snapshots and clones.
entities.decision: Write .fds-<pid>-<name>.tmp in the same directory; check mode, owner, group, xattr names and SHA-256 against the original (and size, for compression) (and, for compression, the compressed flag and the gain); re-read the original's size, mtime, inode and link count; then rename. Any mismatch leaves the original and removes the temp file.

entities.title: Abort after three failures in a row
entities.summary: compress and dedupe stop the run when three files in a row fail.
entities.context: A failure leaves the file untouched, but a run of them suggests something is wrong with the machine or the tool rather than with one file.
entities.decision: Count consecutive failures; reset on success; at three, print `3 consecutive failures - aborting for safety.` and stop.
entities.rationale: Safety, as the message says; the README and the skill tell users and agents to stop on failure while compress and dedupe are untested on real Macs.

entities.title: The daemon counts awake time and skips maintenance wakes
entities.summary: The daemon's cadence runs on a clock that stops while the Mac sleeps, it never schedules a wake, and it skips a check while the display is asleep.
entities.context: A Mac wakes briefly in the background for maintenance with its display off; a cleanup is a burst of disk work and deletion.
entities.decision: Measure the cadence with CLOCK_UPTIME_RAW on macOS; read free space only when CGDisplayIsAsleep says the main display is awake; otherwise log the check as skipped.
entities.rationale: The README names maintenance wakes as the case the display check excludes.
